common._why_permission_mode: bypassPermissions auto-approved sandbox network requests (probe 17.11, Claude Code 2.1.326): example.com reachable. acceptEdits + autoAllowBashIfSandboxed: edits and sandboxed Bash run, anything that needs approval is refused in -p. acceptEdits alone refused interpreters (python3 -m unittest) in -p; settings add permissions.allow ["Bash"] (m-4).

A.about: Sonnet + advisor decides itself; rules and Jev only record

B.about: Rules Engine b-5 enforces R1/R2/R3 via the Stop hook; Jev records

A0.about: Sonnet without the advisor (no --advisor; any advisor call or Opus use makes the run invalid); rules and Jev only record. Diagnostic: effect of the advisor being available, compared with A

Am.about: A with effort medium (a separate, pre-declared condition: does the advisor matter at a smaller reasoning budget); rules and Jev only record

BJ.about: B with R3 gated by Jev (b-6): R1 and R2 block as in B; R3 blocks only when Jev, asked synchronously at that Stop (q-consult-2, jev-1.14.0, threshold 0.5, timeout 10 s), says would_consult; Jev error, timeout or no key: R3 stands (r3_gate_on_error enforce). Jev's time is in the session time, its estimated cost in jev_usd_est

B12.about: Control for BJ: R1 and R2 block as in B, R3 never blocks (recorded as triggered, not_enforced); Jev records

BJd.about: DIAGNOSTIC (BJ-diag), never compared: BJ, but the decision of an R3 that reached the Jev gate is forced to block (r3_gate_force consult). Jev is still asked; its real answer stays in jev_gate.real. Purpose: check the chain R3 block -> advisor call -> answer from the pinned model -> session continues -> Opus cost reconciled (lab.py diag). Left out of pairs and calib.
